Rashi on Gittin 58b:10:3.hebrew: מבני באגא - בני הבקעה; כך היה מנהגם: פוסקים מס על כל הבקעה לתת כך וכך לשנה למלך, והם מחלקין השדות ביניהם, ונותן כ"א מס לפי חלקו המגיעו, ונותנין לאחד והוא נותנו לגבאי המלך. ואם הלך אחד מבני השדות לדרכו, גבאי המלך תובע מבני הבקעה כל המס שלם. והבעלים של קרקע זו הלכו לדרכן, ובני באגא, שהיה כל המס מוטל עליהם, נתנוה לגידול לפרוע המס בשביל הבעלים ולאוכלה:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:10:3.english: From the residents of baga - [That is,] the residents of the valley; such was their custom: [the authorities] assess a tax on the entire valley to give such-and-such [an amount] per year to the king, and they divide the fields among themselves, and each one pays tax according to the portion that falls to him, and they give [it] to one [person], and he gives it to the king's tax collector. And if one of the owners of the fields went on his way, the king's tax collector demands the entire tax in full from the residents of the valley. And the owners of this land had gone on their way, and the residents of baga, upon whom the entire tax was incumbent, gave it to Giddel to pay the tax on behalf of the owners and to consume [its produce]:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:10:4.english: He paid in advance - to the king, the land tax for three years:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:11:1.hebrew: טירפא - שטר מבית דין לטרוף מקרקעות שלהם מה שנתן, שאילו לא באו הבעלים לטרוף ממנו, לא היה מפסיד כלום; ומעתה שיאכלוה אחרים, יטול המלך מנתו מהם ולא יעלו אלה בחשבון, ונמצא זה מפסיד מה שנתן:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:11:1.english: A document of seizure [tirpa] - A document from the court to seize from their lands what he paid, for if the [original] owners had not come to seize [the land] from him, he would not have lost anything; but now that others will consume [its produce], the king will take his portion from them and these [payments] will not be credited to the account, and thus this one [Giddel] ends up losing what he paid:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:11:2.hebrew: אם כן עשית - הדבר כדין סיקריקון, דאמרינן במשנה אחרונה שאינו מפסיד כלום, דקתני: קנה ונותן לבעלים מאי דאוזיל עובד כוכבים גביה, או אם יש בידם ליקח, יחזירו לו מעותיו; והאי נמי לא יפסיד מה שנתן למלך, וגבי כולה. והכא לאו סיקריקון הוא; המלך אין לו עליהם כי אם המס, ומפני אותו החוב נמכרה לזה, ולא היה לו להקדים וליתן של שלש שנים:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:11:2.english: If so, you have made - the matter like the law of Sikarikon, for we say in the later Mishnah that [the buyer] does not lose anything, as it teaches: he acquires [the land] and gives to the [original] owners whatever the idolater discounted for him, or if they have the means to buy [it back], they return his money to him; and this [man] too would not lose what he gave to the king, and [would] collect all of it. Yet here it is not [a case of] Sikarikon; the king has no [claim] against them except the tax, and because of that debt [the land] was sold to this [man], and he should not have advanced [the payment] and given [tax] for three years:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:12:1.hebrew: אמר רב רביע בקרקע או רביע במעות - או יתן לבעלים רביע מעות שנתן לעובד כוכבים, או יתן לו קרקע שוה רביע המעות. אם לקחה במנה, נותן לו רביע מנה, או מן הקרקע עצמו שוה רביע מנה — דהיינו חמישית שבקרקע, אם הבעלים חפצים בקרקע. דקסבר רב: נכי חומשא זבן מן העובד כוכבים — שוה חמש בארבעה. הלכך, יהיב ליה רביע מנה, או חמישית הקרקע, דהיינו רביע מנה, שהקרקע הנקנית מסיקריקון במנה שוה חמשת רביעים. ושמואל אמר: רביע הקרקע עצמו נותן לו, או שליש מנה, דסבר שמואל: נכי ריבעא זבן — שוה ארבע לקח בשלש. הלכך, שדה זו שלקח במנה שוה ארבע שלישי מנה:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:12:1.english: Rav says: one-fourth of the land, or one-fourth in money - Either he gives the [original] owner one-fourth of the money that he gave to the idolater, or he gives him land worth one-fourth of the money. [For example,] if he bought it for a maneh, he gives him one-fourth of a maneh, or [a portion] of the land itself worth one-fourth of a maneh — which is one-fifth of the land — if the owner desires land. For Rav holds [that] one buys [from a Sicarius] at a discount of a fifth from the idolater — [i.e.,] something worth five for four. Therefore, he gives him one-fourth of a maneh, or one-fifth of the land, which is [worth] one-fourth of a maneh, because land bought from a Sicarius for a maneh is worth five-fourths [of a maneh]. And Shmuel says: He gives him one-fourth of the land itself, or one-third of a maneh, for Shmuel holds [that] he buys [at] a discount of a fourth — [i.e.,] something worth four he bought for three. Therefore, this field that he bought for a maneh is worth four-thirds of a maneh:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:14:1.hebrew: זו משנה ראשונה - רישא דמתניתין, דקתני "מקחו בטל":
Rashi on Gittin 58b:14:1.english: This is the initial mishnah - [This refers to] the first clause of our Mishnah, which teaches [that] "his purchase is void":

Rashi on Gittin 58b:15:1.english: Or one-fourth in money - and [this] is difficult for Shmuel:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:16:1.hebrew: כי תניא - רביע במעות, לאחר שבאו שליש המעות ליד הבעלים כשמואל, קרי להו "רביע"; דהא שלשה שלישי נתן לעובד כוכבים ולזה שליש — הרי ארבעה. והכי קאמר: נותן לבעלים רביעית הקרקע, או מעות שיעור שיהו רביע — כשתצטרף של עובד כוכבים ושל בעלים, יהו של בעלים רביע בכולן:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:16:1.english: When [that baraita] is taught - [referring to] a quarter in money: after the third of the money comes into the owner's hand, in accordance with Shmuel, it calls them "a quarter"; for he gave three thirds [of the payment] to the idolater and one third to this [owner] — making four [parts in total]. And this is what it is saying: he gives the owner a quarter of the land, or money in an amount that will be a quarter — [meaning that] when you combine that of the idolater and that of the owner, the owner's [share] will be a quarter of all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג - תניא כוותיה דשמואל:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:1:1.english: The text reads thus - "It is taught in accordance with Shmuel":

Rashi on Gittin 58b:2:2.hebrew: שטר - ולא אחריות נכסים, אלא עד שתכתוב לו שטר, והוה לו לאחריות שאינה יכולה לחזור עליו עוד:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:2:2.english: A bill [of sale] - And not a guarantee of property; rather, [it means] until she writes him a bill [of sale], and this serves for him as a guarantee, in that she cannot come back [with a claim] against him anymore:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:4:1.english: If [he] claims - [meaning] this second buyer [claims] to him [the original owner]:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:4:2.hebrew: מינך זבנה - לוקח ראשון שנתן לך רביע כתקנת בית דין, והדר אכלה שני חזקה, ותו לא מצי אמר ליה האי: "אחזי שטרא", דטפי מתלתא שנין לא מזדהר איניש בשטריה — מאי איריא "חזר ומכרה לאחר"? אפילו לוקח ראשון נמי, בתר דאכלה שני חזקה, אי הוה טעין ליה: "חזרתיה ולקחתיה ממך כתקנת חכמים זה שלש שנים", טענתיה טענה:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:4:2.english: He purchased it from you - [meaning, the second buyer claims that] the first buyer gave you a quarter [of the value] in accordance with the enactment of the court, and then consumed [its produce for] the years of presumptive ownership [chazakah], and this [original owner] can no longer say to him, "Show [your] deed," since beyond three years a person does not take care [to preserve] his deed — why specifically [the case where] "he went and sold it to another"? Even the first buyer himself, after he has consumed [its produce for] the years of presumptive ownership, if he were to claim to him, "I went back and bought it from you in accordance with the enactment of the Sages three years ago," his claim would be a [valid] claim:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:5:1.english: Actually, where he does not claim, and [in a case] such as this - [a case] of sikarikon:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:5:2.hebrew: טוענין ליורש וטוענין ללוקח - הלוקח מסיקריקון, והורישה לבניו ואכלה ג' שנים, או מכרה לאחר ואכלה ג' שנים, ובאו בעלים להוציא ממנו, ואינו יודע לטעון ולומר לו "הראשון קנאה ממך" — בית דין טוענין בשביל היורש ובשביל הלוקח. ואפילו למ"ד במסכת בבא בתרא "אין טוענין ליורש ואין טוענין ללוקח" טענה זו, "הראשון לקחה ממך" — הכא מודי דטענינן ליה, דסתם מאן דזבין מסיקריקון מידע ידע, ולא שדי זוזי בכדי ללוקח אם לא על פי בעלים:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:5:2.english: We make a claim on behalf of an heir and we make a claim on behalf of a buyer - [Where] one bought [a field] from a sikrikon [an extortionist], and bequeathed it to his sons and [the heir] consumed [its produce for] three years, or he sold it to another and [that buyer] consumed [its produce for] three years, and the [original] owners came to extract [it] from him, and he does not know [how] to plead and say to him, "The first [buyer] acquired it from you" — the court makes the claim on behalf of the heir and on behalf of the buyer. And even according to the one who says in [Tractate] Bava Batra [that] "we do not make a claim on behalf of an heir and we do not make a claim on behalf of a buyer" [with] this plea, "The first [one] bought it from you," here he agrees that we make the claim for him; for ordinarily anyone who buys [land that came] from a sikrikon knows [of the extortion], and would not throw away money for nothing [by paying] the [first] buyer unless [it was done] with the consent of the [original] owners:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:6:1.hebrew: ואידך אי טעין אין - אבל לוקח ראשון, אי טעין — אין, אי לא טעין — אנן לא טענינן ליה, דהא ידע אי זבנה אי לא, ואי איתא דזבנה הוה טעין:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:6:1.english: And the other [party], if he claims, yes - However, [regarding] the first buyer: if he claims [that he bought it], yes [he retains possession]; if he does not claim [so], we do not plead [it] on his behalf, for he knows whether he bought it or not, and if it were true that he bought it, he would claim [so]:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:1.english: One who comes due to a debt - [This refers to] an idolater who comes due to a debt [owed by] a Jew:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:2.hebrew: או מחמת אנפרות - גזל בעלמא, ואינו מסור בידו להרוג, ואנס העובד כוכבים קרקעו בחובו או באנפרות:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:2.english: Or due to anparut - [This is] mere robbery, and [the owner] is not handed over into his power to be killed, and the gentile forcibly seized his land for his debt or through anparut:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:3.hebrew: אין בו משום סיקריקון - אם שהה בידו שנים עשר חדש, לתת רביע לבעלים כתקון חכמים ויחזיק בקרקעו; אלא מחזיר לו הקרקע בחנם. דגבי סיקריקון הוא דחזרו ונמנו, דכיון דגמר ואקני אגב אונס מיתה — ואפילו בתר דגזור "כל דקטיל לקטלוה", מסתפי ליה מקמא דקמיה דאקטול — וסופו הוכיח, שהניחה בידו שנים עשר חדש ולא צעק עליו, והלכך נותן לבעלים רביע, דקים להו לרבנן דעובד כוכבים אוזיל גבי לוקח רביע, לפי שבחנם באה לו. אבל האי לא גמר ואקני מידי, ואע"ג דשהתה שנים עשר חדש, לא באת לו שעה לכופו; הלכך אין מכירתו מכירה כלל:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:3.english: It is not subject to [the law of] sikrikon - [that is, the rule that] if it remained in his [the gentile's] possession for twelve months, [the buyer] gives a quarter to the owners in accordance with the enactment of the Sages and retains his land; rather, he returns the land to him without payment. For it was [only] regarding sikrikon that they voted and enacted [this], because since [the owner] resolved and transferred ownership under duress of death — and even after they decreed, "Whoever kills [a Jew] shall be killed," he was [still] afraid of him on account of the earlier ones who killed — and his subsequent behavior proved [his intent], in that he left it in his possession for twelve months and did not protest against him, therefore [the buyer] gives the owners a quarter, for the Rabbis ascertained that the idolater discounts [the price] for the buyer by a quarter since it came to him for free. However, this one [whose land was seized for a debt or through anparot] did not resolve and transfer anything, and even though it remained [in the gentile's possession] for twelve months, no opportunity came to him to compel him [to return it]; therefore, his sale is not a sale at all:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:4.hebrew: צריכה שתשהה - ביד העובד כוכבים שנים עשר חדש, דאי לא — הדרא למרה ויהיב דמי, כדקתני מתניתין: שאם יש בידם ליקח, הם קודמין לכל אדם:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:7:4.english: Must remain - in the possession of the idolater [for] twelve months; for if not, it returns to its [original] owner and he pays the money [to the buyer], as the Mishnah teaches: that if they have [the means] in their hand to buy [it], they take precedence over every person:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:8:1.hebrew: והאמרת אין בו משום סיקריקון - ושנים עשר חדש לא הוזכרו אלא בו, דאילו אנפרות הדרא בלא דמי ולעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:8:1.english: But didn't you say [that the law of] sikarikon does not apply to it - And twelve months were only mentioned regarding [sikarikon], whereas [land taken through] anparut [unjust seizure] returns [to its original owner] without payment, and forever:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:8:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר אנפרות אין בו משום סיקריקון - דאילו מסיקריקון, מוקמינן לה ביד לוקח ונותן רביע; אבל אנפרות, בלא דמי הדרא, ולעולם:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:8:2.english: This is what [it] is saying: [Property taken by] unjust seizure [anparot] is not subject to [the law of] sikarikon - For whereas [when one buys] from a sikarikon [extortionist], we leave [the land] in the buyer's possession and he gives a quarter [of its value to the original owner]; by contrast, [in the case of] anparot, it returns [to the original owner] without payment, and [this applies] forever:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:8:3.hebrew: וסיקריקון עצמה - דאמרינן דקיימא ליה ביד לוקח, והוא ששהתה שנים עשר חדש ביד סיקריקון:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:8:3.english: And [the property of] the Sicarius himself - that we say it remains in the buyer's possession, provided that it remained twelve months in the Sicarius's possession:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:9:1.hebrew: אין אנפרות בבבל - משמע אין עובד כוכבים אונס קרקע מישראל בבבל באנפרות, ואם בא ישראל וערער על חבירו ואומר "קרקע זו שלקחת מן העובד כוכבים שלי היתה וגזלה ממני", אינו נאמן:
Rashi on Gittin 58b:9:1.english: There is no anparut [unjust seizure] in Babylonia - [This] implies [that] an idolater does not forcibly seize land from a Jew in Babylonia through anparut, and if a Jew comes and contests his fellow['s ownership] and says, "This land that you bought from the idolater was mine, and he robbed it from me," he is not believed:

Rashi on Gittin 58b:9:2.english: There is no law of unjust seizure [anparut] in Babylonia - [so as] to cause a loss to the buyer:

Tosafot on Gittin 58b:10:1.hebrew: אנן יהבינן אנן אכלינן - והא דאמרינן בפ' חזקת הבתים (ב"ב דף נד:) גבי דורא דרעוותא, דבני באגי דמטמרי הוו, ומלכא אמר: "מאן דיהיב טסקא ליכול ארעא", והפסידו הקרקע לגמרי — התם היו נשמטים מלפרוע; אבל כאן, שהבעלים הלכו ולא להשמט, דין הוא דכל הנהו שני מאן דיהיב טסקא אכיל, וכי הדרי אהדרי ארעא למרא:
Tosafot on Gittin 58b:10:1.english: We will pay, we will consume - And [as for] that which we say in the chapter [entitled] Chezkat HaBatim (Bava Batra 54b) regarding Dura deRa'avta, where the residents of the valley were hiding, and the king said: "Whoever pays the land tax shall consume [the produce of] the land," and they lost the land completely — there, they were evading payment; but here, where the owners went away and not to evade [payment], the law is that [during] all those years, whoever pays the land tax consumes [the produce], and when they return, they return the land to the owner:

Tosafot on Gittin 58b:11:1.hebrew: למכתב ליה טירפא אבני באגא - לא אבני באגי דקביל מינהון, דמה להן לפרוע מה שהקדים זה, אלא אמרוותא קמאי:
Tosafot on Gittin 58b:11:1.english: To write for him a document of authorization to repossess against the residents of the valley - Not against the residents of the valley from whom he received [the land] — for why should they have to pay what this one [Giddel] advanced? — rather, against the prior owners:

Tosafot on Gittin 58b:12:1.hebrew: רביע בקרקע או רביע במעות - פירוש: רביע במעות שנתן יתן לו, ואותו רביע בקרקע או במעות יתן לו, דהיינו חמישית בקרקע, כדמפר' דנכי חומשא זבין. ותימה: דמאי פריך מברייתא דקתני "רביע בקרקע או רביע במעות" לשמואל, דאמר "רביע בקרקע שהוא שליש במעות", דנכי ריבעא זבין? הא איכא לפרושי נמי איפכא: דרביע הקרקע יתן לו, או בקרקע או במעות, דהיינו שליש מעות! ואית ספרים דגרסי בדרב ובברייתא: "רביע בקרקע שהוא רביע במעות", וכן ר"ח. ומפרש: רביע בקרקע שנתן דמים עליה, דהיינו חומש, דעל ארבע חומשים נתן דמים, דנכי חומשא זבין:
Tosafot on Gittin 58b:12:1.english: One-fourth in land, or one-fourth in money - Meaning: he shall give him one-fourth of the money that he paid, and that [same] one-fourth he shall give him [either] in land or in money, which is one-fifth of the land, as [the Gemara] explains that he purchased [the field] for one-fifth less [than its value]. And this is puzzling: what is [the Gemara's] objection from the baraita — which teaches "one-fourth in land or one-fourth in money" — against Shmuel, who says "one-fourth of the land, which is one-third in money," because he purchased [it] for one-fourth less [than its value]? Surely one can also explain [the baraita] the opposite way: that he shall give him one-fourth of the land, either in land or in money, which is one-third of the money [he paid]! And there are texts that read in Rav's statement and in the baraita: "one-fourth of the land, which is one-fourth in money," and so [reads] Rabbeinu Ḥananel. And he explains: "one-fourth of the land" [means of the portion] for which he paid money, which is one-fifth [of the entire field], because he paid money for four-fifths [of it], since he purchased [it] for one-fifth less [than its value]:

Tosafot on Gittin 58b:5:1.hebrew: כגון זה טוענין ליורש וללוקח - פירש בקונטרס: אפילו למ"ד בב"ב דאין טוענין, הכא מודה. ולא מצינו שם פלוגתא, אלא אמרי' בפרק לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כג.): טוענין ליורש תנינא, טוענין ללוקח תנינא. וכגון זה דאמר, ה"פ: אפילו כגון זה, דסלקא דעתך דהדין עם הבעלים, דמה שלא מיחו, מפני יראת הסיקריקון:
Tosafot on Gittin 58b:5:1.english: In a case such as this, [the court] makes a claim on behalf of an heir and on behalf of a buyer - Rashi explained: Even according to the one who says in Bava Batra that we do not make a claim [on their behalf], here he agrees. However, we do not find a dispute there; rather, [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 23a): "We already learned [in a Mishnah that] we make a claim on behalf of an heir; we already learned [that] we make a claim on behalf of a buyer." And [as for] "such as this" that [Rav Sheshet] said, this is its meaning: even in a case such as this, where it might have entered your mind that the law is with the [original] owners, because the reason they did not protest was out of fear of the sikarikon:
